text:
julia_cs: FYI — customer AtlasFinance opened a P1. They say structured output started failing after our recent model rollout. Their JSON schema validator used to pass but now throws errors (nulls where objects expected, extra keys). Ticket #4642. Posting the customer's sample request/response and repro steps below. :eyes:

omar_ml: thanks — can you paste their exact request payload and the model id they saw? did they pin a model version or rely on latest?

julia_cs: they were calling our hosted generation endpoint with a `response_format` JSON schema. They did NOT pin an explicit version — used `redwood-13b-v2` (latest alias). Customer says last good responses were on 2026-03-11 23:40 UTC, first bad response on 2026-03-12 18:07 UTC (shortly after our rollout). Their request: 

```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-13b-v2",
  "input": "generate invoice summary in JSON",
  "response_format": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "invoice_id": {"type": "string"},
      "total": {"type": "number"},
      "line_items": {
        "type": "array",
        "items": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "description": {"type": "string"},
            "amount": {"type": "number"}
          },
          "required": ["description", "amount"]
        }
      }
    },
    "required": ["invoice_id", "total", "line_items"]
  }
}
```

julia_cs: most recent (bad) response customer pasted: 

```json
{
  "invoice_id": "INV-20260312-9",
  "total": 1250.75,
  "line_items": [
    null,
    {
      "description": "Consulting",
      "amount": 1200.0
    }
  ],
  "legacy_metadata": null
}
```

julia_cs: their validator fails on `line_items[0]` being null and on `legacy_metadata` being an unexpected top-level key. They say prior to rollout they'd never seen `null` placeholders and never had `legacy_metadata` included.

ryan_eng: deploy-bot shows a full rollout of `redwood-13b-v2 -> v2.3` at 2026-03-12T18:05:12Z. `deploy-bot: rollout complete redwood-13b-v2 -> v2.3 (canary -> prod) by @deploy-team`

sre-bot: metric alert — 95p latency for generation API jumped from ~90ms to ~210ms at 2026-03-12T18:05Z (correlates with deploy). No error-rate spike in requests, but more timeouts observed from the customer's side according to their logs.

omar_ml: two immediate hypotheses: 1) a prompt-template/system change in new model introduced an extra trailing token sequence that our structured-output post-processor interprets as `null` placeholders; 2) model vocabulary/tokenization change causing edge-case tokens that our `response_format` serializer mishandles (e.g., emits `null` when a chunk is truncated).

omar_ml: can you include the exact raw text output (not prettified) the customer got? need to see whether model actually emitted the `null` literal or our parser inserted nulls.

julia_cs: pasted from customer (raw):

```
{"invoice_id":"INV-20260312-9","total":1250.75,"line_items":[, {"description":"Consulting","amount":1200.0}],"legacy_metadata":null}
```

julia_cs: they say the first array element in `line_items` is an empty slot (notice the `[,`), which their JSON lib coerces to `null`. They attached their client-side library error: `jsonschema.exceptions.ValidationError: None is not of type 'object' at path /line_items/0`.

omar_ml: that raw output is useful — looks like the model emitted an extra comma (or an empty item) in the array. That can happen if generation policy changed around how lists are serialized (e.g., added trailing commas when enumerating). Need to check decoding behavior and any server-side pretty-print/cleanup transforms.

ryan_eng: quick check of runtime transforms: we have a post-gen normalizer that tries to fix unquoted keys and trailing commas, but it only runs in `schema_strictness: "strict"` mode. The default for this customer is `strict` but it appears the new model variant is sometimes returning mangled tokens that bypass the normalizer because the response length exceeded the token chunk threshold (we recently adjusted chunk size for v2.3 kernels).

omar_ml: actionable repro steps I can run locally — creating a small prompt that instructs the model to output an array with two items and schema enforcement, then sample multiple seeds with temperature 0.0 and 0.2 to see if deterministic. If this reproduces, we can add a quick fix in the post-gen sanitizer to convert empty array slots to omission instead of `null` insertion.

ana_pm: assigning owners — @omar_ml to investigate model-side behavior and run canary evals on the customer's prompt set; @ryan_eng to audit runtime normalizer and chunking threshold change in v2.3. CS to recommend customer pin older model or set `schema_strictness: "loose"` as temporary mitigation.

julia_cs: communicated mitigations to customer: 1) pin previous model digest (we gave them `redwood-13b-v2@2026-02-28`) — confirmed works for them (validation passes again), 2) they can set `schema_strictness: "loose"` to accept `null` entries temporarily, 3) we asked them to forward any further raw outputs if they see more patterns. Customer replied :thumbsup: and bumped to P1 until we root-cause.

omar_ml: next steps for us:
- run batch of 1k synthetic prompts derived from customer examples across `redwood-13b-v2@2026-02-28` and `redwood-13b-v2@2026-03-12` to measure frequency of malformed arrays/trailing commas.
- if repro rate > 0.1%, implement runtime sanitizer that removes empty array slots before schema validation + add telemetry to catch these cases.
- check tokenizer/vocab diffs and any format-level system instruction changes in v2.3 model spec.

ryan_eng: tracking infra change: revert of chunk-size adjustment is possible but risky for perf. Will prototype sanitizer in edge-path (only for `response_format` calls) to minimize blast radius.

julia_cs: I've updated ticket #4642 with the mitigation steps and notified the customer about pinning. Marking thread as "investigating". Will pull in legal/security if we find data-dependent behavior.

omar_ml: I'll post back with the canary eval results within 24h. If we can reproduce deterministically we'll prepare a hotfix for the normalizer.

ryan_eng: logging note — please include the full request_id and the raw generation stream for any future customer examples. It makes triage much faster.

julia_cs: thanks team. I'll keep the customer updated and unlock any extra logs for engineering. :lock:
